note: PRE reproduced and frozen BEFORE any edit. All five findings are mine.

E1_absent_identity_reaches_the_port.verdict: an identity absent from the fresh order book was returned as verified, submitted to cancel_order, and a forged outcome string released the gate. The check today required neither presence nor the evidence type.

E2_outcomes_untyped.verdict: a bare dict of strings released the gate — no bytes, no source, no timestamp, no parser, no policy binding, no venue identity.

E3_blind_reissue.scenario: crash mid-close; the position CHANGED (qty 10 -> 20) while the executor was down
E3_blind_reissue.verdict: the unacknowledged close was re-issued with no position identity, no side/units, no reduce-only contract and no idempotency key, against a changed position — and the plan completed.

E4_concurrent_resume_duplicates_the_clos.verdict: two concurrent resumes both observed close_requested without close_acknowledged and BOTH called the port. The journal refused the second acknowledgement, but the venue had already received two closes — per-record O_EXCL does not lock the read/reconcile/effect transaction.

POST.E1: presence is REQUIRED for every named identity still awaiting acknowledgement, with role entry, in fresh open-order evidence of the RIGHT KIND; duplicates refuse; positions evidence cannot stand in for an order book. Presence gates only unacknowledged cancellations — an acknowledged one is absent precisely because it was cancelled, and the terminal evidence judges it, never absence. The ghost identity now stops before any port call.
POST.E2: terminal verdicts are a sealed evidence type, terminal_orders, parsed from original venue bytes for BOTH venues (Alpaca canceled/expired/filled/rejected/replaced/failed; MT5 ORDER_STATE_CANCELED/EXPIRED/FILLED/REJECTED). Only a venue-declared terminal status yields a verdict; absence never does; a non-terminal status refuses at the parser; a bare mapping raises ExecutorError; stale terminal evidence stops the plan; the gate journal carries the evidence provenance (type, raw_sha256, parser_digest, venue_direct).
POST.E3: the close binds the exact position — identity, side, units, reduce_only, and a durable idempotency key derived from the plan — persisted in the journal before the port is called. Resume reconciles FIRST: flat evidence confirms without reissue; a changed or multiplied position is never closed by replay; a port that does not declare same_key_idempotent_reduce_only never gets a reissue; the same position through a declaring port is retried with the SAME key, and the acknowledgement records reissued_with_same_key. More than one open position refuses — ambiguous exposure is never closed blind.
POST.E4: a per-plan run lock covers the whole reconcile-through-acknowledgement transaction. A held lock is a typed PlanLockHeld; a lock left by a dead process is an operator disposition, never an automatic takeover; the lock releases on success and on stop. Proven with threads AND two real processes at a file barrier for all three boundaries: the ambiguous submit issues NOTHING (0 effects), the cancel boundary issues exactly one cancel (plus the winner's single legitimate decision), the close boundary exactly one close; all effects come from ONE process and the lock refuses exactly one claimant.
POST.E5: the plan is a digest-verified envelope with schema lts.effect_executor.plan.v1; six tampered fields each refuse, and a self-consistent reforge still fails the live directive recheck. Custody idempotency reads the record through a typed exists() and verifies the complete binding; 'in str(exc)' no longer appears in the module, asserted structurally. Custody transitions carry a durable monotone executor event ordinal (the verified journal length); a test asserts requested_at_bar >= 1 and confirmed_at_bar > requested_at_bar.

mutation_check: disabling the absence check, the sameness guard, the port-contract guard, the lock's exclusivity and the plan digest together broke 11 tests; green on revert.
